title: Questions, information and answers - what must be settled before any decision is reasonable
rule: an answer is only written here when a specific official page was read in this session; otherwise the answer stays blank and the row says what would fill it

blocks.blocking: a decision cannot be made until this is answered
blocks.shaping: the decision can be made, but the answer changes its size or order

rows.question: What will market prices come from, given the league publishes none?
rows.know: No official nfl.com odds page exists in any read recorded in this repo or this session; every price column in peer namespaces is blank or labelled THIRD-PARTY.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner will license a feed, accept third-party captures permanently, or run price-independent forever.
rows.discovery: a written verdict on SG-01; nothing technical is missing

rows.question: Is a third-party archive an acceptable source for a number that is quoted on the site?
rows.know: Peer namespaces hold nflverse-derived captures and label them THIRD-PARTY, CC BY 4.0; the brief says 'verify everything from official verified trusted sources'.
rows.dont_know: Whether 'trusted' includes third-party archives for prices, since 'official' cannot.
rows.discovery: one owner sentence; then the label rule is written into the publication contract

rows.question: Which namespace is the canonical dashboard the owner reviews?
rows.know: 22 NFL namespaces exist in this repo at the base commit, each with its own index and tables; the reviewer's brief does not name one.
rows.dont_know: Which one is authoritative, so the same requirement is currently met 22 times in slightly different ways.
rows.discovery: pick one namespace as canonical; everyone else becomes an appendix

rows.question: What exactly does 'the 136-game log' refer to?
rows.know: The official standings arithmetic gives 145 games credited to date, 133 through Week 9, 147 when Week 10 completes; no file in the repo publishes 136.
rows.dont_know: The log the owner means - a prior session's file, a spreadsheet outside the repo, or a stale count.
rows.answer: partially resolved: 136 is not reproducible from any repo file or from the official standings at read time; the three reproducible counts are published instead (data/derived/standings_check.json)
rows.discovery: the owner names the file; or accept 133/145/147 as the corpus definition

rows.question: Where does an ordered depth rank exist that we are allowed to store?
rows.know: nfl.com publishes no team depth-chart page (peers recorded a 404); the brief forbids inferring rank from jersey order, experience or salary, and forbids transcribing a club's image by eye.
rows.dont_know: Any authorized structured source with a rank per slot per club.
rows.discovery: either a licensed data agreement or a written decision to use snap-share from game books as the only rank proxy

rows.question: Do official game books parse into a participation list we can use for 'who actually did start'?
rows.know: The game centre publishes a 'Download Game Book (PDF)' link; one was read and its URL recorded this session (fixture 2 of 14).
rows.dont_know: Whether every fixture publishes one, and whether the participation section is machine-parseable at 272-game scale.
rows.answer: partially resolved: the link exists and is a stable per-game asset for the fixture checked; the parser is not written
rows.discovery: open the other 13 game centres, then write the parser against one week before anything is fitted

rows.question: What is the report's own update cadence, in hours, rather than the rulebook's deadlines?
rows.know: Between the 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 renders, 11 rows changed designation, 6 changed practice status and 11 gained or lost an injury label - concentrated in LAC (10 of 11) plus one IND clearance, with zero rows added or removed.
rows.dont_know: Which submissions (Saturday or Sunday-morning) produce that movement, because we have two adjacent renders, not a daily series.
rows.answer: partially resolved: the movement is measurable and dated; the mechanism needs a 5-day series
rows.discovery: capture daily Wed-Kickoff for 2 weeks and diff each pair

rows.question: Is the record printed beside a team on the injury report a pre-game attribute or a live join?
rows.know: For all 28 clubs on the report the bracketed record equals the LIVE standings record at read time, including clubs whose games were still in progress; the report prints W-L and appends -T only when a tie exists.
rows.dont_know: : whether the record ever lags during a game (it did not on the day measured).
rows.answer: resolved: it is a live join. It must be stored with the read's clock time and never treated as a property of the availability snapshot
rows.discovery: none needed - measured 28/28

rows.question: Does the injury report list every player a club has?
rows.know: No. Absences verified this session: Malik Willis (IR) and Kyle McCord (healthy, expected starter) appear in no MIA row; the report shows only designated players, 11 for Miami.
rows.dont_know: An official per-club roster+IR endpoint on nfl.com that this session did not open.
rows.answer: partially resolved: 'not listed' is proven to mean nothing about availability (EV-06, EV-07)
rows.discovery: fetch one club roster page and one IR list, then define the join key

rows.question: How stale can a report row be, and in which direction?
rows.know: Daiyan Henley is on LAC's Week 10 report five days after both clubs announced his trade to Denver (EV-01, EV-02). The report is not roster-versioned.
rows.dont_know: Whether removals happen on a fixed day or only when the club submits nothing.
rows.discovery: one week of daily captures joined to the transactions hub - then the staleness distribution is measurable

rows.question: Can a designation ever be read as a severity signal?
rows.know: No, as published: Puka Nacua's report row leaves the Injuries cell blank while a dated official item says IR with three named injuries; eight NYG players have injuries named in Tuesday's news text and blank injury cells in the report.
rows.dont_know: How often the two disagree across a season.
rows.answer: partially resolved: two worked contradictions measured in one week
rows.discovery: count label-presence per designation over a season

rows.question: What should a model do with 'Not injury related - resting player' and '- personal matter'?
rows.know: These strings appear in the official Injuries column (JAX 2, LAR 1, HOU 1, LAC 1 = 5 rows this week, computed by engine/capture.py) and they are not injuries; a feature that counts injury labels would treat them as one.
rows.dont_know: Whether the league classifies them consistently across clubs or whether it is free text per club.
rows.answer: partially resolved: counted, with the vocabulary published; the classification question stays open
rows.discovery: census across a full season, then decide whether they enter a model at all

rows.question: Where do void/push rules for parlays and prop combos come from?
rows.know: Nothing in the repo stores operator rules; the joint-evidence gate therefore cannot be satisfied by any currently available data.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner will supply terms, or whether the project treats combos as out of scope.
rows.discovery: a written rules source per operator, or drop combos from the roadmap

rows.question: Which numbers may the leaderboard show before n=300 is reached?
rows.know: Peer runs report 0 of 8 strategies qualifying against a floor of n>=300, largest sample 77; the brief forbids backtest numbers on the leaderboard.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner wants a 'provisional, unranked' tier visible at all.
rows.discovery: a decision on showing unranked provisional rows (SUG-04)

rows.question: Is the removal-of-luck panel computable without prices?
rows.know: Two of the four components (opponent adjustment, league base rates) are computable from the standings and results; two (CLV, realised ROI) are not.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner accepts a two-component panel labelled as incomplete, or wants the panel withheld until prices exist.
rows.discovery: a verdict on SUG-06

rows.question: Do raw row-level injury rows belong on a public page?
rows.know: The brief asks for all entries in table form on a public GitHub Pages site; one requirement asks for a private data layer until terms are read.
rows.dont_know: The league's position on redistribution, which has not been read.
rows.discovery: read the terms for /injuries/ and write the verdict; the site keeps or moves the table accordingly

rows.question: What is the four-club hole in the report, and is it a defect?
rows.know: CHI, DEN, PHI and TB have no section in the Week 10 report; the schedule page's own 'Teams on Bye' block lists exactly those four, so the hole is explained by the schedule, not by a missing capture.
rows.dont_know: : nothing further for this week - this is resolved for Week 10 and must be re-checked every week.
rows.answer: resolved for Week 10: 28 sections + 4 byes = 32 clubs, reconciled against the official bye block
rows.discovery: none - but the reconciliation must be automated, and it is (engine/audit.py)

rows.question: Where do the depth figures in the brief come from (149 multi-rank-1 slots, Texans image, Packers jersey numbers, 2 shared/empty slots)?
rows.know: No file at the base commit publishes any of those numbers, and they cannot be reproduced from anything in the repo; they reference a depth-chart dataset this repo does not contain.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner is quoting an external tool or an earlier working state that was never committed.
rows.discovery: the owner attaches the depth dataset, or these requirements are re-scoped to the sources that exist

rows.question: Where do the Week 10 figures in the brief come from (254 vs 279 rows, 4 vs 2 no-injury sections, 6 of 254 designations, CIN 4 players)?
rows.know: This session measured 347 rows / 28 sections / 0 sections without an injury label / 171 designated rows; a peer capture on 2026-11-14 measured 347 rows identically. nfl-audit holds 276 rows with 6 designations, nfl-arena 326 with 25.
rows.dont_know: Which store produced 254 or 279, and why CIN was quoted as 4 players where both the 11-14 and 11-15 renders show 9.
rows.answer: partially resolved: the claim is unreproducible and the closest repo figures are published beside it
rows.discovery: the owner names the source, or the figures are retired from the brief

rows.question: Is a two-day gap between captures enough to treat a report as immutable?
rows.know: Two renders 24 hours apart differ in 11 designation rows; three older renders differ by whole clubs (nfl-audit is missing 2 club sections, nfl-arena by 21 rows).
rows.dont_know: The intra-day behaviour (the final Friday report at 4 PM ET is the rule; the page does not print its own revision time).
rows.discovery: capture twice on one Friday, one hour apart - the cheapest test in the queue

rows.question: What does the site owe the owner between now and Week 11's report?
rows.know: Week 11's report will appear with its own Wed/Thu/Fri cycle; nothing in the repo can produce it on a schedule, because no collector runs.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner will run a scheduled job (GitHub Actions on a cron is available in this repo) or continue to accept manual captures per agent session.
rows.discovery: a decision on SUG-02 (schedule the collector) - the code half is done, the schedule half is not

rows.question: Which fixtures does the venue requirement actually cover?
rows.know: 14 fixtures in Week 10; the schedule card prints a venue for none of them in text - one game centre printed 'MUNICH / FC BAYERN MUNICH STADIUM' and two hotel locators named Paycor Stadium and M&T Bank Stadium.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner wants per-game pages opened for all 272 fixtures of the season, or only for the slate being priced.
rows.discovery: scope decision: full-season (272 fetches, mechanical) or pricing-week only (14 per cycle)

rows.question: Is a news-headline record good enough for announced starters, or must the article body be read?
rows.know: For Lock, McCord, Watson and Beck the headline plus URL read inside the official report page was enough to name a starter; the bodies were not opened this session.
rows.dont_know: Whether the bodies contradict or narrow the headlines (e.g. 'expected to start' vs 'will start').
rows.answer: partially resolved: headline-grade evidence is recorded as headline-grade in evidence.json - the confidence label matches what was read
rows.discovery: open the bodies for the 5 announced-starter items when a model actually consumes them

rows.question: Do we accept the repo's own negative result about our lines?
rows.know: A peer namespace published, on the site, that originated lines are worse than market lines on 105 walk-forward games (spread MAE 9.383 vs 8.814; total 11.112 vs 10.357) and awarded 0 of 1,000 reward units.
rows.dont_know: Whether the owner wants the origination effort to continue on that evidence, or to pivot to availability-only indices for a year.
rows.discovery: a decision on SUG-07; the number itself is not in dispute because it is reproducible from the repo
